spec.title: IED security documentation survey: catalogue inventory
spec.note: Rules that turn each vendor's own catalogue listing into inventory entries. A rule reads one field: 'url', 'slug' (last path segment) or 'text' (model name and, where the vendor gives one, its one-line product type; during enrich, the product page's title and opening words). The first matching rule wins and an exclusion always beats a category. Lifecycle values are the states fixed under 'definitions'; a rule may add 'vendor_label' to keep the vendor's own word (legacy, obsolete, active mature) without letting it decide the state. A lifecycle_text rule reads the product page and may carry 'within', the number of opening characters it looks at, so that a notice about one variant further down the page does not mark the whole product. Change a rule and re-apply it with: survey.py inventory --from <previous inventory>.

definitions.legacy: A device is counted as legacy when the vendor states, in a dated source, that it has been discontinued: manufacture or sale has ended, whether support continues, has ended or is not mentioned. The three lifecycle states that make up the group are also counted one by one, so a device whose support has ended can still be told from one that is only no longer sold. The protocol a device speaks, a security feature it lacks, the age of its manual and the vendor's own use of the word legacy never decide this.

lifecycle_statuses.currently_supported: Listed in the vendor's current catalogue on the inventory date without a notice of discontinuation, or stated by the vendor to be on sale and supported. Not legacy.
lifecycle_statuses.discontinued_supported: The vendor states that manufacture or sale has ended and that support continues. Legacy.
lifecycle_statuses.discontinued_support_not_stated: The vendor states that manufacture or sale has ended; no statement about support was found. Legacy.
lifecycle_statuses.end_of_support: The vendor states that support has ended. Legacy.
lifecycle_statuses.unknown: None of the above is established. This includes products the vendor only labels legacy, products under a last-time-buy notice and families that are partly withdrawn. Not counted as legacy, because nothing dated says the device has been discontinued.

definitions.release_date: Recorded separately when a vendor source states it. It never decides lifecycle status.

revisions.change: Legacy widened from the end-of-support state alone to every device the vendor has discontinued.
revisions.known_then: A first review of the 99 sampled devices, drafted by an AI assistant and not confirmed by the author, had been counted under the earlier definition. It placed no device in the legacy group, because no public vendor page states an end of support, and 31 devices in the group "discontinued, support not stated". The author then decided that discontinued devices count as legacy. The sample, the documents and the review rows are the same before and after; only the grouping changed.
